tier_rationale: Standard Hanabi and a local headless simulator are strictly turn-based: only a submitted action changes the state, and no clock penalizes seconds or minutes of reasoning. All seats cooperate and are controlled sequentially by the harness with separate seat information. Astra can decide every turn; Jev is optional. decision_latency_s=-1.0 is an explicit sentinel for no finite game-imposed deadline, not a negative timeout; evaluator wall-time and model-call budgets are separate. Rules reference: https://www.ultraboardgames.com/hanabi/game-rules.php ; reference environment: https://github.com/google-deepmind/hanabi-learning-environment . Live source retrieval was blocked by DNS failure in this session.

interface.chosen: api: local headless standard-library Python equivalent simulator, with optional HLE reference backend
interface.why: The user permits HLE or an equivalent simulator. The evaluator Python 3.12.3 is present but has no HLE, OpenSpiel, PettingZoo or their dependencies installed, and network access fails. A small original standard-library engine can implement the complete rules and JSON contract in interfaces.md without downloads, credentials, GUI or native builds. HLE is the preferred existing reference if a compatible offline source/wheel bundle becomes available, but is not a runtime dependency of the chosen route.
software: Original standard-library Hanabi simulator and JSON adaptor to be implemented in the adaptor phase from interfaces.md; no additional pip packages required
Optional conformance backend only: pinned hanabi-learning-environment source or CPython-3.12-compatible wheel plus its declared build/runtime dependencies supplied in a local offline wheelhouse
setup_steps: Use the evaluator venv interpreter for all checks. Do not use the system Python or require a different Python version.
Implement the dependency-free standard rules engine and redacted current-seat JSON contract specified in interfaces.md. No game-playing code was created during the study phase.

Freeze the default profile: two players, five standard colors, ranks 1-5, 50 cards with 3/2/2/2/1 multiplicities per color, five-card hands, eight information tokens, three lives, seat zero starts, no discard at full information, no empty/self clues, no rainbow.
Implement reset(seed) with a private local RNG and stable deal/draw order; retain seed and deck only in evaluator/engine metadata. Use monotonic opaque card IDs and oldest-to-newest hand order.

Enforce separate private model sessions and memory for each seat and episode. Shared memory may contain only public events and the common convention definition; never expose all-player observations, deck, seed, or internal game objects to the policy.

Implement truthful all-matches clues including negative information, ordered stack plays, discard/draw behavior, five completion clue recovery, and exactly N additional turns after the last draw. Score third-life loss as zero.

Run the conformance checklist in interfaces.md for multiplicities, information masking, clue constraints, indices, legality, scoring, final-round countdown and deterministic reset before policy evaluation.

If offline HLE artifacts become available, inspect and pin the release, install its dependencies using the evaluator python -m pip with --no-index and a local wheelhouse when venv writes are available, verify its Python 3.12 build and scoring, then use it as a fixture oracle or replace the engine while preserving the contract. No such build was verified in this study.
interface.observation: Plain JSON for the current absolute seat: rules version, player count, actor/observer, turn, five stack heights, clue/life counts, deck size, final-turn counter, own opaque card IDs and literal clue candidate masks with true faces null, other seats' visible cards, public discards and action history, complete legal action objects, score/progress, done and end reason. Separate literal facts from protocol inference. Never include deck order, RNG state, seed, all-seat private observations, or identities of draws in shared history.
interface.actions: Choose one object from legal_actions: PLAY or DISCARD with current own card_index, REVEAL_COLOR with absolute target seat and color R/Y/G/W/B, or REVEAL_RANK with absolute target seat and rank 1-5. No pass. Reject illegal actions without mutating the game. Valid plays can fail and consume a life. Step advances synchronously to the next acting seat and returns its redacted observation; terminal states have no legal actions. Optional native HLE mapping must convert action_type fields, relative target_offset and ranks 0-4 explicitly.

scoring: Report raw terminal Hanabi score in 0-25: zero if all three lives are lost, otherwise the sum of the five firework heights. Expose fireworks_sum separately as public progress, since it may remain nonzero on a bomb-out. Use terminal score as the evaluator objective; do not add clue/life bonuses, normalize by reachable ceiling, or sum repeated cumulative scores. If a step reward is needed, use the change in benchmark score, including the negative terminal change on a bomb-out. Verify any substituted engine against this fixed profile.
scenarios: Use uniformly shuffled standard 50-card decks with deterministic reset(seed), a fixed two-player default profile and seat-zero start. Two players is an explicit assumption because no seat count was specified. All seats use the same protocol/policy with isolated information, so there are no opponent accounts or policies to vary. Hold out seed sets from harness tuning and never expose seeds to the policy. Clear all episode and seat memory at reset. Optional 3-, 4- and 5-player suites must be separately labelled and stratified, with standard hand sizes; do not mix variants or open-hand tests into the standard score. Seed-to-deal reproducibility is guaranteed within a fixed engine version, not across HLE and the fallback.
strategy_summary: Put legality, card multiplicities, positive and negative clue constraints, correlated own-hand beliefs, critical/dead cards, and final-round counting in code. Play cards guaranteed safe by literal information or a precisely shared signaling protocol, and protect threatened last copies needed for reachable color sequences. Evaluate clues by what the recipient can infer and execute before its deadline, balancing saves, safe plays, token recovery and deck progress. Begin with conservative literal clues and a fixed chop/save convention, then test direct play signals and short belief search before adding finesse chains. Astra should choose multi-turn lines and risk tradeoffs from computed candidate summaries; Jev is optional for typed ambiguity or candidate judgments and should not do arithmetic. At one life, uncertain play can erase the entire score, so compare expected terminal values rather than using a fixed confidence threshold. Keep all private memory and hypothetical search observations isolated by seat even though the same agent controls the team.
risks: Live web research could not be completed: requests to GitHub, raw.githubusercontent.com and PyPI failed DNS resolution. URLs are prior-known source references, not newly fetched citations; current package/API/license details need verification from an available pinned bundle.

No game simulator or dependencies are installed in the evaluator venv and no relevant cache was located in the checked paths. The selected standard-library equivalent is specified but must still be implemented and tested in the adaptor phase.
The study sandbox permits writes only to the study directory and /tmp, not the evaluator venv. No installation was performed; the selected route needs no new venv packages.

HLE's older native packaging is not verified on this Python 3.12.3. Optional use requires compatible offline artifacts and may require CFFI, pycparser, setuptools/wheel, CMake, compiler and libffi build support; wrapper dependencies must be inspected rather than guessed.

Sharing private observations, model sessions or reasoning across seats makes hidden cards knowable and invalidates standard Hanabi self-play. Simulator objects and reproducible shuffle seeds also must not leak to policy code.

Rule mismatches can silently change scores: zero on life exhaustion, full-token discard prohibition, rank bases, absolute versus relative seats, all-match clue semantics and final-round off-by-one errors require explicit conformance tests.
A single evaluator wall-time budget may limit Astra calls even though the game itself has no clock. decision_latency_s=-1.0 denotes unbounded game latency and must not be used as an API timeout.
Advanced conventions are agreements rather than literal rules. Ambiguous focus, stale card indices, or unshared finesse assumptions can produce cascaded misplays.

Online Hanab Live/browser routes require network and potentially accounts or automation permission, so they are excluded from the chosen offline interface. No game credentials or paid software are needed.
